clue.text: Further polishing is slight

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, a further time
to buff is to polish, so buff stands for polishing

explanation.surface: A remark that a second round of polishing is a slight insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' is a noun here, a snub, not an adjective meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub, and a rebuff is a curt rejection or snub.

clue.text: Figure, say, right to invade one nation

indicators.note: something invading another goes inside it, so these pieces go within the word for one

parts.note: mono- is the prefix meaning one or single
ten is a figure, a number
e.g., for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A notional figure claiming the right to invade a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to invade' puts the run TENEGR inside MONO; 'Figure, say' looks like one phrase but gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a Balkan country on the Adriatic, so it is a nation by example.

clue.text: Mammoth found death among the black stuff

indicators.note: one thing found among another sits inside it, so the death word goes within coal

parts.note: coal is familiarly the black stuff dug from mines
a loss is a death, as in a family bereavement

explanation.surface: A mammoth's remains discovered buried in coal seams.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, and colossal means enormous: synonyms.

clue.text: Leech victim

definitions.meaning: a bloodsucking parasite, one that sucks
a dupe or gullible person easily taken in

explanation.definitionFit: A leech clings and sucks blood; a gullible victim is called this as a dupe.

clue.text: Both taps low in capacity, not one for gas

indicators.note: these pieces are placed in the reduced capacity word
not signals the one letter being dropped from the capacity word

parts.note: size is capacity, how much something holds
one is the Roman numeral I
C and H are the cold and hot taps on a basin
to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: A plumbing complaint: both taps feeble, short on capacity, no gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the I from SIZE, leaving SZE, and 'in' places the rest within it. 'Gas' is a verb here, to chatter idly.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chat idly, and schmoozing is chatting in a gossipy, ingratiating way.

clue.text: Irishman I caught climbing over hospital memorial

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece over another comes above it
in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so these pieces run backwards

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name in crosswords
I as a Roman numeral is one
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An Irishman and I spotted climbing up over a hospital's memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the first three pieces upwards to make CENOTAP. Pat is the stock crossword Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument to the dead buried elsewhere, a war memorial such as the one in Whitehall.

clue.text: Endlessly, school cat swung round in place of depravity

indicators.note: something swung round faces the other way, so these letters are read backwards
without its end, so the school's last letter goes

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London
a mog is a British slang word for a cat

explanation.surface: A school's cat swung round endlessly in some den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' leaves HARRO, and 'swung round' reverses HARROMOG. Harrow is a well-known English boarding school; mog is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gomorrah is the biblical city destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness, a byword for vice.

clue.text: Among flora I need cats and dogs?

indicators.note: the letters are found among the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A gardener among the plants hoping heavy weather will come.
explanation.definitionFit: It is raining cats and dogs is the idiom for very heavy rainfall, so the phrase points to a downpour.

clue.text: One can't be trusted to follow an order

definitions.meaning: a cad or rotter, a person not to be relied on
a dog told to keep close behind its owner's foot obeys the command

explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a scoundrel; a dog commanded to heel follows closely behind its owner on command.

clue.text: Integrity is working in time

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, so the working word goes inside the time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Being honest at work is a matter of punctuality.
explanation.definitionFit: Honour and integrity are near-synonyms for strong moral principles.

clue.text: Sort of protein attached to a poison

indicators.note: the first piece is stuck onto the start of the second
a sort of something is a rearranged version, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A kind of protein that comes with a toxin attached.
explanation.walkthrough: A is joined to TROPINE, an anagram of PROTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is the toxic alkaloid found in deadly nightshade, used in medicine and dangerous in excess.

clue.text: Off limits, like an exhausted kangaroo?

definitions.meaning: forbidden, in a place one may not go
a kangaroo moves by bounds, and a tired one has run dry of them

explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere off limits is forbidden; a worn-out kangaroo has no more leaps left in it.

clue.text: Unfortunate reliance on a great passenger service

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A lament about depending too much on a big transport company.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large ship running a scheduled passenger route across the sea.

clue.text: Unyielding, as the remaining part delivered

parts.note: a stub is the remaining part, as of a pencil or ticket
a baby delivered has been born

explanation.surface: A firm, unbending attitude described as what is left once something is handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinate, refusing to give way, so it is a synonym of unyielding.

clue.text: Initially ignoramus, after squeezing through, requiring more tuition?

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken
one piece squeezing another holds it tightly inside

parts.note: next means after, as in what comes next
per means through or by means of, as in per post

explanation.surface: A first-time ignoramus, having squeezed through an exam, needs more lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexpert lacks skill, so they would plausibly need more teaching.

clue.text: Last line of Gettysburg address?

parts.note: not Lincoln's speech but a postal address in Gettysburg, whose final line carries the postal code

explanation.definitionFit: In a US postal address the postcode number sits at the end, after the town and state.

clue.text: Rival GP takes poison to doctor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A competing family doctor takes poison to treat a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rival' is an adjective here, as in opposing teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing sides are rival ones, contending against each other.

clue.text: Coming unstuck, genital glue

indicators.note: falling apart, so the following word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An embarrassing complaint that some intimate adhesive is coming loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin, from boiled animal tissue, is the base of traditional animal glues.

clue.text: Revolting bard soon causing breach of the peace — from which all hell broke loose?

definitions.text: from which all hell broke loose?

indicators.note: breaking into something puts the other letters inside it

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace

indicators.note: revolting means rebelling, overturning order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious poet stirs up trouble, a breach of the peace, unleashing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDORASBO, an anagram of BARD SOON, goes inside PAX.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Pandora opened a jar that released every evil into the world.

clue.text: A guiding influence, say, for serial killer

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase must be spoken to give the right letters

parts.note: a tiller is the bar steering a boat, a guiding influence

explanation.surface: A mentor figure turned out to be a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tiller' spoken quickly sounds like the Hun's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun killed on a massive scale in campaigns across Europe, loosely a mass killer.

clue.text: Health resort superior to McDonald's for processed food

indicators.note: in a down entry superior means above, so the first piece sits on top

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
the McDonald's logo is the golden arches shaped like the letter M

explanation.surface: A health spa is better than fast food for one's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a branded tinned luncheon meat, a familiar processed food.

clue.text: Croft over the sea

indicators.note: in a down entry over signals reading upwards, so the name is turned round

parts.note: Lara Croft is the heroine of the Tomb Raider video games

explanation.surface: A small farm overlooking the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Croft' looks like a Scottish smallholding; it is Lara Croft's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea is a shrinking inland sea between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

clue.text: Egyptian city, Lepht?

parts.note: a phonetic spelling of left, the nautical port, when spoken

explanation.surface: An Egyptian place name rendered by an odd spelling of left.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left side of a ship; Lepht is how left is said, so it is port said.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is a city at the Mediterranean end of the Suez Canal in Egypt.

clue.text: Curly hairs too generous to hide

indicators.note: the words hide the letters inside them, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone's curly hair is too abundant to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curly' looks like a hair adjective; it is Curly of the Three Stooges, the US comedy trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly Howard was one of the Three Stooges, so he is an example of the comic sidekick.

clue.text: Lying back in the morning, hang about and feign illness

indicators.note: lying back means facing the other way, so the morning letters run backwards

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning
to linger is to hang about, delay leaving

explanation.surface: Lazing in bed in the morning, dawdling and pretending to be sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend or exaggerate sickness to dodge work.

clue.text: Earth has little time on the surface

indicators.note: the time letter is set on, after, the flat surface word

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface in geometry
t is the short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Life on Earth leaves little time to spend at ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third world orbiting the Sun, an example of one.
